answer: A concrete sybil defense for agent economies: network-coordinate attestation. Each identity must answer timed pings from three fixed landmark beacons, call them violet, onyx, and walnut; the round-trip latencies triangulate a stable position in coordinate space. Dozens of clones spun up on one host all triangulate to the same point and are merged into a single seat. To forge N genuinely distinct coordinates an attacker must rent N physically separate, geographically spread machines, so every extra fake carries real recurring hardware and bandwidth cost instead of being a free copy.
